nodes.title: Duality for perfect local systems
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, U a locally spatial diamond and L in D_ét(U,Λ) an étale-locally constant complex with perfect Λ-module values. Then L is dualizable, its dual is L^∨ = Rℋom_Λ(L,Λ_U), this dual is again a perfect local system, and the evaluation-induced map L^∨ ⊗^L_Λ A → Rℋom_Λ(L,A) is an equivalence naturally for every A in D_ét(U,Λ). Evaluation and coevaluation satisfy the two triangle identities. This statement requires neither a cohomological-dimension bound nor noetherian coefficients.
hypotheses: Use the enhanced closed symmetric monoidal étale category, at a sufficient fixed cutoff, and its homotopy category.
Local constancy means an étale covering trivializes L with perfect values; no single global perfect value is required.
proofSteps: Form the dual using C3/internal-hom and the canonical evaluation comparison. C5/etale-extension-by-zero supplies the projection formula, hence compatibility of internal Hom with étale restriction; arbitrary pullback compatibility is not assumed.

Choose an étale trivializing cover. On each member the constant-complex functor is symmetric monoidal. Import perfect-module duality and the perfect tensor–Hom equivalence from P7; this makes the canonical comparison an equivalence on each member, including with arbitrary A.

Use C2/v-hyperdescent (and its étale specialization) to reflect the equivalence on the cover. The dual restricts to the constant perfect module dual, so is itself a perfect local system. The adjunction and this natural comparison give evaluation and coevaluation, with the triangle identities checked on the same conservative cover.
For C9 use j! ⊣ j* to obtain derived Hom(j!L,B) ≃ RΓ(U,L^∨ ⊗^L j*B). Tensor and pullback preserve coproducts; the uniform cohomological bound is needed only for the RΓ factor.
acceptance: For L=Λ_U the comparison is the unit constraint A≃Rℋom(Λ_U,A).
For constant finite projective complexes, recover the supplier’s tensor–Hom map, including its Koszul convention.
The constant complex Q over Z is excluded: local constancy without perfect values cannot replace the hypothesis.
The proof does not depend on general-coefficient perfect-constructible v-descent (E11), a spatiality assumption on U, or a finite cohomological bound.

sources.locator: Proposition 20.17, last paragraph, pp.121–122; Proposition 20.16(iii), pp.120–121

nodes.title: Compact closure of a recurrent field automorphism
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete nonarchimedean normed field and γ a norm-preserving field automorphism. Suppose that for every x in C, γ^(n!)(x) tends to x as n tends to infinity. Give the automorphisms the topology induced by their underlying functions in C^C. The integer action n↦γ^n extends uniquely to a continuous action of the profinite completion of Z by norm-preserving field automorphisms. Its image is precisely the pointwise closure of the integer powers, and this image is a compact procyclic profinite group. The closure of the nonnegative powers is the same set. In particular it is compact as a subset of C^C.
hypotheses: Completeness is for the given norm, which satisfies the ultrametric inequality.
The factorial-power convergence is pointwise, for every field element; convergence at a chosen generating subset is not substituted.
Algebraic closedness and positive characteristic are not required for this compactness lemma.
proofSteps: For x in a finite set F and ε>0 choose N≥1 such that ‖γ^(N!)(x)−x‖<ε for every x in F. Telescoping, the ultrametric inequality and isometry give ‖γ^(mN!)(x)−x‖≤‖γ^(N!)(x)−x‖ for every integer m; negative m follow by applying the inverse isometry. If a−b is divisible by N!, the same estimate bounds ‖γ^a(x)−γ^b(x)‖.

Give Z the profinite group uniformity. The preceding estimate says every orbit map Z→C is uniformly continuous. Use the existing completion and extension API to extend the orbit maps to the profinite completion. In this specialization the inverse limit of Z/dZ is the separated uniform completion: residues modulo N! form a cofinal basis and make the integers totally bounded. Completeness of C supplies the limits; no compactness of norm-bounded subsets of C is assumed.

Extend the ring laws and the norm equality by density. To establish the action law, for a,b in the completion approximate both by integers. Isometry bounds the error from moving the input of γ^a separately from the pointwise error at the fixed input; this proves joint continuity of evaluation and passes γ^(a+b)=γ^a∘γ^b to the limit. The values at a and −a are inverses, so a limit is a surjective automorphism, not merely an isometric field embedding.

The image is compact in the Hausdorff product C^C. Density identifies it with the closure of integer powers. The kernel is closed; the quotient of the existing profinite completion by this closed normal subgroup is profinite by the pinned quotient theorem. The compact-to-Hausdorff bijection identifies that quotient topology with the image topology. Nonnegative integers are also dense modulo every positive integer, so the same image is the closure of nonnegative powers.

In Lemma 21.17, triviality on leading terms first implies norm preservation. Its condition ‖γ(x)/x−1‖<1 for every x≠0 passes to the image because open ultrametric balls are closed. The general procyclic power and Sylow calculus is imported, not reconstructed as a field-specific group theory.
acceptance: For γ=id the image is a singleton and is compact.
For a norm-preserving finite-order automorphism, the image is its finite cyclic group; the factorial hypothesis holds.
Account explicitly for inverse automorphisms and the continuity of composition on the isometry image.
Retain the given pointwise topology and distinguish the compact closure from an infinite abstract cyclic subgroup.

sources.locator: Lemma 21.17, first paragraph of proof, p.127

nodeRefinements.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond and Λ a commutative ring, and suppose that one natural number N satisfies H^i(Y,F)=0 for every i>N and every étale Λ-module sheaf F on Y. For a quasicompact separated étale map j:U→Y and a perfect local system L on U, the object j!L is compact in D_ét(Y,Λ). The same N bounds cohomology on U by C9/uniform-test-bound.
nodeRefinements.reason: Replace the stage-level API placeholder by the named duality lemma, state the single cohomological bound explicitly as a vanishing condition above N, and cite the lemma in the proof steps.
proofSteps: The adjunction j! ⊣ j* of C5/etale-extension-by-zero and the C3 internal Hom identify derived Hom(j!L,−) with RΓ(U,Rℋom_Λ(L,j*−)); C7/perfect-local-system-dualizable identifies this with RΓ(U,L^∨⊗^L_Λ j*−).
Pullback j* is a left adjoint, and tensoring with L^∨ preserves coproducts (E1 derived tensor, C3/etale-tensor).
By C9/uniform-test-bound the same N bounds the cohomology of every étale Λ-module sheaf on U, so C9/global-sections-coproducts makes RΓ(U,−) commute with coproducts.

The leading-term assumption implies that γ is an isometry. Apply compact-procyclic-field-action: the closure G of the powers of γ is a compact procyclic profinite group, and its last step passes all the leading-term congruences to G. If G is not pro-p, some quotient G/U by an open normal subgroup has order divisible by a prime ℓ≠p. Take a Sylow pro-ℓ subgroup H of G (pinned TauCeti.exists_isProPSylow). Its image in G/U has index prime to ℓ (IsProPSylow.not_dvd_index), so H is nontrivial; H is pro-ℓ (IsProPSylow.isProP) and compact, being closed in G.

Choose x≠0 moved by H. The continuous function h↦‖h(x)/x−1‖ attains a maximum δ on compact H. Since all leading-term congruences hold, 0<δ<1. Choose h0 attaining δ and set y=h0(x)/x−1, so y≠0 and ‖y‖=δ. For every h, d_h=h(x)/x−1 satisfies ‖d_h/y‖≤1; the residue map c(h)=res(d_h/y) is defined on all of H and c(h0)≠0.

For g,h∈H use d_(gh)=d_g+g(d_h)+d_g g(d_h). Every g acts trivially on the residue field and has g(y)/y≡1. Therefore res(g(d_h)/y)=res(d_h/y). The cross term divided by y has norm at most δ<1, so c(gh)=c(g)+c(h). The residue field is discrete because its maximal ideal is open, hence c is continuous.

The pinned IsProP.isPGroup_range says the image of c is an ℓ-group even for an infinite discrete residue field. Its elements are killed by p. IsPGroup.orderOf_coprime and ℓ≠p force that image to be trivial, contradicting c(h0)≠0. Thus the compact procyclic group is pro-p; finite p-group quotients show its p^n powers tend to the identity, and point evaluation gives the result.
